title: Signal Index — Standup Catalog (2028-11-30)
content:
Context: weekly roll-up that acts as a compact catalog of what each day surfaced across tracing, dashboards, and cost telemetry. Intention: make standup items searchable and actionable (index-style), reduce repeated status threads, and highlight experiments that change span volume or ingestion cost.

This week (Mon 2028-11-26 -> Thu 2028-11-29) — highlights
- Sampling experiment (cohort-based): reduced default ingest sample from 0.2 -> 0.05 for non-error traces on user-facing routes. Early result: spans ingested/day dropped ~38% (baseline 9.6M -> 6.0M). Pipeline CPU usage on tracing-ingest decreased ~22% during peak.
- Dashboard tidy: consolidated 4 heatmap tiles into a single "latency-by-cohort" tile; simplified query to use aggregated_span_latency which cut dashboard query time by ~40%.
- Cost telemetry micro-scrub: identified 3 customers where tracer re-emission increased tokenized payload size due to verbose tags; suggested schema contract to devs to truncate large baggage fields. Estimated immediate 6% savings on span-export egress for those accounts.

Daily standup catalog (short entries, owner, quick status)
- Mon 2028-11-26 — Diego: sampling rollout plan and smoke tests. Status: canary on staging, looks stable. Blocker: missing synthetic traces for streaming route, added synthetic generator ticket OBS-4123.
- Tue 2028-11-27 — Kira: dashboard refactor completed for latency tiles; reworked reduce-cardinality pipeline to squash high-card tags. Status: review pending on PR 1284.
- Wed 2028-11-28 — Martin: cost telemetry scrub run; produced per-customer egress report and short list of top-5 offending tag keys. Status: outreach to Solutions for customers with custom SDKs.
- Thu 2028-11-29 — Ava: rollout decision meeting; moved sampling plan to staged rollout across regions eu-west1 then us-west2. Status: rollout scheduled 2028-12-03.

Experiment details (sampling cohort)
- Hypothesis: lowering sample rate for non-error, non-high-QPS cohorts reduces cost without materially changing SLO observability for backend errors.
- Method: mark spans with cohort tag (cohort: low-qps | med-qps | high-qps | errors). Only low-qps default sample reduced. Errors always sampled 100%.
- Early metrics (3 days canary):
  * Low-qps spans ingested/day: 3.2M -> 0.9M (-72%)
  * Observability alert noise (false positive paging) on error-budget SLOs: +1 instance (investigating noise source — likely sampling alignment with synthetic traffic)
  * Ingest cost delta (raw): -34% on tracing pipeline spend for canary hosts

Decisions made
- Proceed to staged rollout; preserve 100% sampling for any span with tag error=true, user-impacting=true, or contains-exception=true.
- Add synthetic trace generator for streaming route (ticket OBS-4123) — provides deterministic error traces for canary verification.

Open action items (owner, ETA)
- Diego: finish synthetic generator + integration tests. ETA 2028-12-02.
- Kira: address PR review comments on reduce-cardinality pipeline (PR #1284). ETA 2028-12-01.
- Martin: draft customer outreach note for top-5 egress offenders and propose SDK truncation pattern. ETA 2028-12-04.
- Ava: coordinate region rollout schedule with infra (eu-west1 -> us-west2), open infra-change (CHG-obs-20281203). ETA 2028-12-01.

Blockers / risks
- Risk: sampling misalignment with internal synthetic traffic may cause SLO alerting gap during rollout. Mitigation: synthetic generator + extra canary monitoring for 48 hours post-rollout.
- Risk: downstream consumers (third-party exporters) depend on full tag set; trimming tags may break them. Mitigation: add deprecation timeline and export compat shim for 2 months.

Quick metrics snapshot (timestamped 2028-11-29 17:30 UTC)
- Spans ingested (7d median/day): 8.9M
- Pipeline CPU p95 (canary hosts): 1.7 vCPU -> 1.3 vCPU (after canary)
- Tracing pipeline egress cost (daily): $1,260 -> projected $840 with rollout
- Dashboards: average query duration before refactor 1.1s, after 0.64s

Notes to self / informal scribbles
- If we drop sample rate too aggressively we need a fast kill switch (route-level override via feature flag). Add a front-line playbook step.
- Consider adding a "sampling telemetry" dashboard tile that shows sample-rate vs alert-rate over time per cohort. Helpful for on-call.

Appendix — useful queries and dashboard tiles (summaries, not full SQL)
- "aggregated_span_latency": uses precomputed histogrambuckets by service+cohort — used by new latency-by-cohort tile.
- "egress-by-tag-key": group by tag_key, sum(payload_bytes), filter top 20; used to identify verbose baggage.
- Canary verification checklist (manual + automated):
  1) synthetic trace generator emits expected error traces for streaming route;
  2) error-rate SLOs remain within baseline +/-10% for 48h;
  3) no new paging alerts triggered in on-call channel.

Unresolved questions / follow-ups
- Should we expose per-customer sample-rate in the Console (billing transparency)? Product feedback requested from Solutions.
- Long-term: can we do adaptive sampling that reacts to anomaly score rather than static cohort? Put on backlog for R&D (ticket OBS-RD-29).

References / links
- OBS-4123 (synthetic generator) — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OBS-4123
- PR 1284 — reduce-cardinality pipeline refactor — https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/1284
- Confluence playbook draft — confluence:Observability/Signal-Index-Playbook

End of catalog entry. Quick ask: reviewers, please add comments inline for PR 1284 and flag any customer compatibility concerns for tag truncation before 2028-12-04.

Short checklist for next standup (2028-12-03)
- Diego: canary generator deployed to staging? (Y/N)
- Kira: PR review merged? (Y/N)
- Martin: customer outreach note posted? (Y/N)
